The age (4–8 years) and pattern of referred knee pain are classic for a pediatric hip disorder rather than primary knee pathology. Absence of fever, normal vital signs, and no systemic symptoms make septic arthritis or inflammatory arthropathy unlikely. Radiographs showing flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head are characteristic of avascular necrosis of the femoral head in children. Differential (transient synovitis, SCFE, trauma, tumor) is less likely given the imaging and clinical picture. Therefore the most likely diagnosis is Legg–Calvé–Perthes disease (idiopathic osteonecrosis of the femoral capital epiphysis) of the left hip.

DIAGNOSIS: Legg–Calvé–Perthes disease (left femoral head avascular necrosis)
